acceptance_criteria.criterion: The persona build system resolves models for all three suites using the priority chain: `assignments.json persona_models[persona_id]` > per-persona YAML `model`/`model_slug` > `_shared.yaml` `default_model`/`default_model_slug`
`cc_model` is resolved per persona from the registry entry matching the assigned model UUID, falling back to `_shared.yaml` `cc_model`
When a persona is assigned the `inherit` model, VS Code frontmatter omits the `model` field entirely
When a persona is assigned the `inherit` model, Claude Code frontmatter uses `model: 'inherit'`
The build functions correctly when `assignments.json` and `local.json` do not exist (graceful fallback to current YAML-only behavior)
The `{{#if model}}` conditional is applied only to VS Code frontmatter templates — Claude Code templates always render their `model:` line

summary: Implemented model assignment override in personas/plugins/ledger/index.js: added loadModelRegistry() function that reads local.json (falling back to default.json) and assignments.json from personas/model-registry/; module-level cached registry loaded at import time; ledgerPlugin() factory accepts optional registryDir override for test injection.

Replaced the old simple YAML fallback logic (model → default_model, model_slug → default_model_slug) in onBuildContext with a full 5-step priority chain: (1) assignments.json persona_models[id] UUID→slug, (2) per-persona YAML model_slug, (3) assignments.json default_model_uuid UUID→slug, (4) _shared.yaml default_model_slug, (5) inherit sentinel (model='', cc_model='inherit').

Updated FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_VSCODE in frontmatter-templates.js to wrap model field with {{#if model}} conditional — omits the field when model is falsy (inherit case); CC template unchanged (always renders model: line via CC_FRONTMATTER_FIELDS).
Added 11 new tests in ledger-plugin.test.js covering AC-1 through AC-6 and the inherit sentinel behavior; all 118 tests pass; build --check passes (120 personas, byte-identical output).

comments.note: personas/plugins/ledger/index.js: The module-level registry is loaded once at import time from MODEL_REGISTRY_DIR. This is efficient for production but means registry changes mid-process (e.g. during watch-mode builds) won't be picked up without a process restart. For the current single-pass build workflow this is fine, but if watch-mode is ever added, the registry loading should move into onBuildStart or equivalent.

personas/plugins/ledger/frontmatter-templates.js: The {{#if model}} conditional places model: on the same line as the block opener and role: immediately after {{/if}} with no blank line separator. Depending on how the template engine handles whitespace around conditionals, this may produce subtly different whitespace when model is absent vs present. The build --check passes, confirming the current form is byte-identical with the committed output, so this is safe as-is.

personas/plugins/ledger/index.js: The loadModelRegistry() function duplicates similar logic from scripts/lib/persona-model-resolution.js (loadModelRegistry there). The two are not DRY — the plugin version is CJS and uses fs/path directly; the scripts version is ESM. If the registry loading logic ever needs to change (e.g. new file format), both must be updated. A shared CJS-compatible lib would reduce this duplication, but requires a careful dependency graph review.

comments.note: personas/plugins/ledger/index.js (priority chain): The 'inherit' sentinel at per-persona assignment level (step 1) correctly falls through to the next priority level. This means a persona explicitly assigned 'inherit' will resolve to the default_model_uuid if one exists. This is correct per the test fixtures (test at line 730-741 confirms this fall-through behavior), but the AC wording 'When a persona is assigned the inherit model, VS Code frontmatter omits the model field entirely' could mislead reviewers into expecting the omission unconditionally. The actual behavior (inherit falls through) is intentional and consistent with the test suite.

scripts/tests/ledger-plugin.test.js: The AC-3 and AC-4 tests (lines 664-683) test the 'inherit model omits field' case using an EMPTY context (no default_model_slug). This means the test only exercises the full-inherit scenario, not the fall-through scenario. A follow-up test explicitly verifying the fall-through behavior (inherit per-persona + default_model_uuid present = default_model resolves) could make the intent clearer, though this is covered by the test at line 730-741.

No test exists for the case where `persona_models` key is present in assignments.json but maps to a UUID that does not map to any slug in the registry (i.e., uuidToSlug.get(uuid) returns undefined). The code correctly falls through (resolveFromSlug is never called), but an explicit test for this case would add coverage. Edge-case manual test during QA confirmed correct behavior.

summary: [PASS] Code review complete for WP-005 (Persona Build System Model Resolution Override). All 6 acceptance criteria confirmed met. The priority chain in onBuildContext is correctly implemented and well-documented. Template conditional ({{#if model}}) is correctly scoped to VS Code only. Graceful fallback logic is robust. One Fix-Forward applied (comment precision). No blocking issues found.

comments.note: personas/plugins/ledger/index.js (lines 227, 244): The fall-through comments read '// slug === inherit → skip, fall through' but the guard `if (slug && slug !== 'inherit')` also handles the undefined case (unknown UUID in registry). Updated both comments to '// slug undefined (unknown UUID) or inherit → skip, fall through' for accuracy. Non-behavioral — identical runtime logic.

personas/plugins/ledger/index.js vs scripts/lib/persona-model-resolution.js: Two loadModelRegistry() implementations coexist — one CJS (plugin), one ESM (scripts lib). The divergence is intentional given the module system boundary (build-personas.js is ESM; the plugin is CJS). The key behavioral difference to preserve: the scripts lib version emits console.warn on malformed JSON (lines 62–64, 75–76), while the plugin silently swallows the error. The scripts lib behavior is preferable for maintainability — if the plugin is ever ported to ESM or a shared lib becomes feasible, the warn path should be preserved.

scripts/lib/persona-model-resolution.js resolveModel(): The slugToEntry Map is rebuilt from registryEntries on every call (lines 116–121). For the current single-pass build workflow this is negligible, but if resolveModel is ever called in a tight loop (e.g. 1000+ personas), the Map construction cost will appear in profiles. Pre-building slugToEntry in loadModelRegistry() and returning it alongside uuidToSlug would eliminate the rebuild. Low priority — not a blocking concern.

[documentation-forward] personas/plugins/ledger/index.js loadModelRegistry() docblock: The function's @returns JSDoc lists `uuidToSlug` and `slugToEntry` but the documentation should clarify that `slugToEntry` maps slug → full registry entry object (not just slug → name), and note that the silent error-swallowing on malformed JSON is intentional for production build resilience (vs the scripts lib which warns). This distinction helps future maintainers understand the design intent without reading the scripts lib for comparison.

[documentation-forward] personas/model-registry/README.md: The 'Orchestrator' bullet in the 'Inherit / Auto Sentinel' section notes it 'Skips the assignment and falls back to YAML-based resolution.' This is accurate but could be more precise — it falls through to the YAML model_slug at step 2, then default_model_uuid at step 3, then _shared.yaml at step 4, before applying the inherit sentinel at step 5. A brief note about the 5-step priority chain (or a link to the plugin onBuildContext comments) would help operators understand exactly what 'falls back to YAML-based resolution' means in practice.

All 6 ACs verified green. Build --check passes (120 personas, byte-identical). 118/118 tests pass.

Key behavioral note for reviewer: 'inherit' at per-persona assignment level is a fall-through sentinel, not an unconditional override. A persona assigned 'inherit' will still pick up the default_model_uuid if configured. Only when no model is configured at any level does the final inherit sentinel apply (model='', cc_model='inherit'). This is correct per the test fixtures.
Edge cases verified: malformed JSON files in registry dir, unknown UUIDs, personas without id field, local.json overriding default.json — all handled gracefully without errors.
Developer's note about module-level registry caching (improvement comment in implementation pipeline) is valid but low-risk for the current single-pass build workflow.

All 6 ACs confirmed met. The priority chain implementation in onBuildContext is clean and well-commented. The {{#if model}} conditional in FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_VSCODE correctly omits the model field for VS Code when the inherit sentinel applies; the CC template always renders its model: line via CC_FRONTMATTER_FIELDS.

One Fix-Forward applied: comment precision improvement in the Step 1 and Step 3 fall-through guards (non-behavioral — purely clarifies that undefined/unknown UUID is also handled by the guard, not just inherit slug).
